purpose: Teach: ルピー/一室/座敷/刺す/ザル/ローテーション/そりゃあ/ちまう

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、本気で、絶対、お父さん、絶対、海外旅行で、絶対、ルピー、絶対、両替したぞ、覚えてる?本気で
lines.en: Gran, do you remember? When Dad was young, he went overseas and exchanged money into rupees—he really did.
lines.style: Soft opening. Gentle nostalgia threading through each phrase. Slow, unhurried pace. Slight lift on the memory itself, as if testing it's still there. Warm but tentative.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: うん。若い頃、本気で、絶対、家の、絶対、一室、絶対、お祖父ちゃんの、絶対、書斎、絶対、だったわよね、覚えてる、あなた?本気で
lines.en: Yes, I do. You know, when your grandfather was young, one room in the house was his study—do you remember that, dear?
lines.style: Matching his softness but with more certainty. Each memory lands like she's placing it carefully. Slight warmth on the recollection. Unhurried, intimate.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 若い頃、本気で、絶対、お客様、絶対、座敷、絶対、お父さん、絶対、お通ししたぞ、覚えてる、ばあさん?本気で
lines.en: When Dad was young, he used to show guests into the tatami room—do you remember that, gran?
lines.style: Quieter than before. Each image offered gently, not insisted upon. Pace slows further. Searching her face a little. The tenderness of checking if she's still there with him.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: 若い頃、本気で、絶対、お裁縫の針で、絶対、ばあさん、絶対、指を、絶対、刺す、絶対、こと、絶対、ありましたわよね、覚えてる、あなた?本気で
lines.en: Oh yes. When I was young, I used to prick my fingers with the sewing needle more times than I can count—you remember that, don't you?
lines.style: Light tease underneath the nostalgia. Small, genuine laugh threaded in. Not mocking—affectionate. She's offering him a moment of lightness. Warm and slightly mischievous.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 若い頃、本気で、絶対、ばあさんの、絶対、ザル、絶対、お蕎麦、絶対、お父さん、絶対、大好きだったぞ、覚えてる?本気で
lines.en: Your zaru soba—when I was young, Dad loved that so much. Do you remember?
lines.style: Voice softens on the food memory. Genuine appreciation surfaces. Slower still. The specificity lands with weight—he's tasting it again. Slight trailing-off, like he's lost in it.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: 若い頃、本気で、絶対、お祖父ちゃん、絶対、お仕事の、絶対、ローテーション、絶対、しっかり、絶対、組んでいたわよね、覚えてる、あなた?本気で
lines.en: When Grandfather was working, we kept the rotation schedule so carefully put together—do you remember that, dear?
lines.style: Practical warmth underneath. Pride in the small details, the way they kept things running. Steady pace. Not performative—just stating what was solid and true. A little strength in her voice.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: そりゃあ、本気で、絶対、若い頃、絶対、お父さん、絶対、ばあさんに、絶対、感謝、絶対、していたぞ、覚えてる?本気で
lines.en: Of course. When Dad was young, he was truly grateful to Gran—he really was. Do you remember?
lines.style: Conviction arrives here. Not wistful anymore—direct. Simple and clear. The gratitude is stated as fact, not as sentiment. Eyes steady. A little firmer in the voice.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: 若い頃、本気で、絶対、お祖父ちゃん、絶対、お味噌汁、絶対、飲んじゃうしちまう、絶対、こと、絶対、ありましたわよね、覚えてる、あなた?本気で
lines.en: Oh, your grandfather would drink the miso soup right up—there were so many times he did that—do you remember, dear?
lines.style: Tender laugh in the voice. The fond exasperation of someone remembering their partner's small appetite. Slight acceleration on the drinking-up bit. Warm and present, not distant. Intimate.
